newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude differentials gain as margins recover.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude differentials gain as margins recover.

text.p: North Sea sweet crudes responded to improved refining margins as differentials continued to creep up in active trade on Tuesday.
Although Brent looked cheap at current levels, traders looking at the arbitrage possibilities to the U.S. saw limited upside.
Outright May Brent on the IPE recovered some recent losses but failed to hold above $18 and traded up 14 cents at $17.90 a barrel by 1700 GMT.

With Brent cargoes offered at up to May -80 cents and offers at May -90 cents, the market continued to be manipulated but the upside was limited to 10-15 cents, in a market still fundamentally long, traders said.

"We just don't see the arb (to the U.S.). There are small positive margins at the moment but if I look three weeks ahead we are looking at negative margins. The upside is limited," one U.S. refiner said.

At least five million barrels of sweet North Sea crude changed hands on Tuesday. A cargo of Brent moved early at May Brent -92 cents for an April 15-17 loader but the seller took back an April 19-21 cargo at a dated related number.
Two or three third decade April Ekofisk cargoes moved at between dated Brent +3 to +5 cents. A cargo moved last Wednesday at dated -3 cents.

A VLCC of Oseberg was seen going transatlantic taking earlier sloppiness out of the market and the crude traded at a five cent discount to dated Brent for an April 21-23 loader. There were unconfirmed reports of an end month cargo moving to a refiner at dated Brent -4 cents. A prompt (Apr 15-17) sold at dated Brent -10 cents.
One buyer was seen picking up three Forties cargoes at dated evens and dated Brent +1 cent.

"I think we have seen the bottom of the market as far as dated Brent is concerned. It looks pretty cheap compared to the other grades....there is still some upside on some grades but the May cargoes are just around the corner," an equity holder commented.
Both Brent April 23-25 cargoes were kept on Tuesday. One was expected to be put on the spot market while the other may end up in the U.S., traders said.

Brent intermonth spread activity concentrated on the May/June where one buyer picked up two of the four spread trades done at -21 cents. The same buyer was heard to have picked up a May/June earlier in the day at -23 cents.

CFD trade was thin on the ground with talk on next week's April 14-18 dates at a firmer June -68/-65 cents. Action was concentrated further out with the April 28-02 trading at June -48 and -50 cents and April 28-02 moving at June -45 and later at June -44 cents.
In the Mediterranean Urals held firmer though no trade was reported. Short term limited availabilities saw even buyers talking around dated Brent -$1.30/-$1.25 a barrel.
